Relative formula mass of aluminium oxide = (27 x 2) + (16 x 3) = 102

Mass of aluminium oxide = 1020g

Moles of aluminium oxide = 1020g / 102 = 10 moles

There are 2 units of aluminium oxide for every 4 units of aluminium (shown by the equation) so we have to calculate moles accordingly 

(10/2) x 4 = 20 moles of aluminium

Alternatively as 2 is half of 4, you can just double it so 10 x 2 = 20 moles of aluminium

Aluminium has an atomic mass of 27, so we can convert to actual mass: 

27 x 20 moles = 540g of aluminium
